To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the worst-case analysis of the game-theoretic interpretation of loss minimization leads to parameter-free aggregation algorithms that are as efficient as those for convex loss minimization but work for many nonconvex loss functions, and (ii) the resulting algorithms are margin-based in a general sense, but without the usual assumptions on margin distributions.

(i) the game-theoretic framework for loss minimization provides an elegant way to understand the behavior of aggregation algorithms; and (ii) the worst-case performance guarantees that follow from the game-theoretics are surprisingly strong, and lead to efficient algorithms that work for any loss function in the class of convex surrogates.

the best aggregation algorithm for a broad class (including but not limited to) all convex surrogaces is the same algorithm that minimizes a generalized notion of margin, and this algorithm can be implemented efficiently using a linear predictor.
